name: NemTokenV2 counts any transfer into the pair as a sell and lets anyone burn the pending amount out of the pair
summary: NemTokenV2 treats every transfer into its NEM/USDT PancakeSwap pair as a sell and queues the net amount in pendingLpSellRecycle, and the public flushLpSellRecycle() burns 70% of that queue (capped at 20% of the pair's balance) from the pair and syncs it, with no check that a swap settled. With flash-loaned USDT the attacker transferred NEM into the pair, skimmed it back and flushed, 42 times, burning down the pair's NEM reserve, then sold NEM for the pair's 821,920 USDT.
notes: Reset is the token's deployment, which also created the pair; the only later admin writes the exploit read are the trade and profit tax recipients (setTradeTaxAddresses/setProfitTaxAddresses, about 3 hours later) and the owner's renunciation, fee recipients and ownership that rule 8 does not count.
Loss is the pair's USDT; about 95,600 USDT of it went to the PancakeSwap pools the attack contract flash-borrowed from. The pair's 53.1m burned NEM is valued at nothing (rule 12).

The attacker's four earlier helper contracts (e.g. 0x0c3dac1d, 0xa16f9a31) reverted on their attack call and were only emptied back to the attacker. campaign.mjs finds no earlier external flushLpSellRecycle call; two later ones by 0x8d952fa3 (block 129155055) burned 16 NEM and moved no USDT.
